svg.title: YOLO11n-seg step-by-step calculation
svg.desc: Nine animated steps: preprocessing, one convolution block, backbone, neck, head, box decoding, non-max suppression, prototype masks and mask assembly.

g.text: Make the photo a fixed-format tensor the network can read
Resize keeping aspect ratio, pad the short side with gray (letterbox), scale to 0–1 and reorder to channels-first.
At predict time only a multiple of 32 is needed (here 640×448). Training uses square 640×640 batches.
Step 2 of 9 · One Conv block, calculated
Every layer of the backbone is built from this: Conv2d → BatchNorm → SiLU
Repeat with C_out different kernels → C_out channels
(16 kernels in the first layer, 256 in the last)
The kernel slides over the input two cells at a time (stride 2). Each stop multiplies and sums the 3×3 window.
BatchNorm re-centres the result, SiLU adds the non-linearity. The grid shrinks 2× per strided Conv.
Step 3 of 9 · Backbone: downsample and enrich
Spatial size shrinks, channel count grows; three maps are tapped (P3, P4, P5)
split channels, run small bottlenecks, concat, 1×1 Conv
self-attention on half the channels → global context
Each strided Conv halves height and width (448×640 → 14×20, total stride 32) while C3k2 blocks add depth.
The n-model uses width ×0.25 and depth ×0.5, so channels top out at 256 instead of 1024.
Step 4 of 9 · Neck (PAN-FPN): mix the scales
Top-down brings meaning to fine maps; bottom-up brings detail to coarse maps
Top-down: upsample the deep map and concatenate it with the shallower one (channels add), then fuse with C3k2.
Bottom-up: a strided Conv shrinks the map again and concatenates it. Outputs: 64@56×80, 128@28×40, 256@14×20.
Step 5 of 9 · Segment head: predict at every cell
Three parallel branches turn each feature vector into box, class and mask outputs
Same head design on P4 and P5 (separate weights)
Candidates = cells of all three grids
Every grid cell proposes one object: 64 numbers describe its box edges, 80 the class scores, 32 the mask recipe.
No anchors: the cell itself is the starting point. Nothing has been filtered yet.
Step 6 of 9 · Decode one candidate into a box + score
Raw head numbers are turned into pixels and probabilities
① softmax over 16 bins per edge (DFL), then take the expected value
② distance × stride, measured from the cell centre
The box is expressed in input-image pixels (448×640 space).
③ class score = sigmoid(logit): σ(2.2) = 0.90 → “person” (80 scores per cell, take the max)
④ the 32 mask coefficients are carried along unchanged for step 9.
The box branch outputs a probability distribution over distances, not a single number, which makes edges more accurate.
This is repeated for all 5,880 candidates in parallel (it is just tensor maths).
Step 7 of 9 · Filter and Non-Max Suppression
Many cells fire on the same object; keep the best box per object
① Keep cells whose best class score ≥ 0.25
② Per class: sort by score, keep the best
person: A 0.90 first · bus: E 0.95 first
③ Drop boxes with IoU > 0.7 against a kept box
④ Cap at 300 detections; survivors go on
Neighbouring cells all predict almost the same box. NMS keeps the highest score and removes boxes that overlap it too much.
IoU = overlap area ÷ union area. These IoU values are computed from the drawn boxes; counts are illustrative.
Step 8 of 9 · Prototype branch: build the shared mask basis
Runs in parallel to the head, starting from the P3 output (finest scale)
halves, centre-surround… learned by the network.
• Computed once per image, shared by every object.
• Not tied to a class: a mask is a mix of them.
Objects only differ in their 32 coefficients,
so extra objects cost almost nothing.
A small stack of convolutions plus one upsampling step turns the 56×80 feature map into 32 maps of 112×160.
This idea comes from YOLACT: predict basis masks once, then combine them cheaply per object.
Step 9 of 9 · Assemble the instance masks
Combine the shared prototypes with each object’s own 32 coefficients
① Take the 32 coefficients of the kept detection (person A) and mix the prototypes:
② Turn it into a clean object mask:
Repeat for every kept detection; the whole image was processed in one forward pass.
Weighted sum of 32 prototype maps → sigmoid → crop to the detected box → resize to the photo → threshold at 0.5.
Output per object: class, confidence, box and a pixel mask. Cheap, because the heavy part was shared.
